title: A Safe Launch: From Supervision to Trust and Independence
summary: Before your child leaves your home, your task is to transition them from control to trust: they make their own decisions, bear their consequences, and know you are a support, not a watcher. Entrust them with real responsibilities in money, time, and commitments, and keep your door and heart open no matter how they err; for the youth who finds a home that embraces them will not seek acceptance in the wrong places.
try_this: This week: Hand over to your child a decision that was in your hands (managing an amount of money, organizing time, a commitment), agree on its boundaries, then give them the space to execute and learn from the outcome without interference.
reflection_prompts: What real responsibility did you hand over to your child this week?
How did they handle it, and what did you learn from it?

review_defects.arabic: كيف تعامل معها، وبماذا تعلّم منها؟
review_defects.english: How did they handle it, and what did you learn from it?
review_defects.why: The Arabic asks what the child learned (تعلّم منها), but the English asks what the parent learned. This changes the focus from the child's learning to the parent's learning.

review_defects.arabic: ابنك (your son) and masculine singular pronouns throughout
review_defects.why: The Arabic specifically addresses a son using masculine forms, while the English uses gender-neutral language. This loses the original's masculine specificity and may alter the intended audience.
